profile.lede: I work with open sources, and I care about what can honestly be concluded from them.
paragraphs: I’m a computer science student at Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology (GGSIPU), reading B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering with a CGPA of {grade}. My focus sits in cybersecurity research — open-source intelligence, threat intelligence and breach analysis.

My interest in this field started with a personal experience of cyber fraud. Understanding how information gets collected, exposed and turned into risk gave me a reason to focus on the defensive side, and it still shapes how I work: careful investigation, evidence-based analysis, ethical research, and findings written up clearly enough for somebody else to act on.
The material I publish comes from public sources, CTF exercises and my own analysis of publicly reported incidents. I would rather publish a small finding I can defend than a large one I cannot.

project.title: Dark Web Threat Intelligence Engine
project.overview: The engine is a background collector for Tor hidden services. It crawls the onion sites you configure, filters what it finds against a keyword set, extracts indicators of compromise, asks a local language model whether a post is actually relevant and what it is about, stores the result, and pushes the matches to a chat channel. It runs on a schedule and keeps its own record of what it has already seen.
project.problem: Threat-relevant posts are spread across services that are slow to browse, awkward to search and impossible to monitor consistently. The practical result is that the same pages get re-read over and over, and the genuinely new material is easy to miss in the noise.

features.title: Tor onion service crawling
features.body: Crawls configured onion services asynchronously through a local Tor SOCKS5 proxy, following links up to a configurable depth and page limit.

features.title: Keyword pre-filtering
features.body: Target keywords are read from the `KEYWORDS` environment variable. With `LLM_PREFILTER_KEYWORDS` enabled, page text is screened for those terms before any inference runs, so irrelevant pages cost nothing.

features.title: Local LLM classification
features.body: A local model classifies threat relevance and writes concise incident summaries. Nothing is sent to an external API, so the material being collected stays on the machine.

features.title: Indicator of compromise extraction
features.body: Extracts cryptocurrency addresses (BTC legacy, SegWit and Bech32, ETH, XMR, LTC, BCH), contact handles (Telegram, Tox, Keybase, email), v3 onion URLs, PGP key blocks and SHA-256 hashes from raw page text.

features.title: Deduplication and retention
features.body: Content hashes are stored in SQLite and enforced through deduplication indexes, so the same post is not alerted on twice. Records older than the retention window are purged.

features.title: Telegram alert dispatch
features.body: Relevant findings are queued and delivered as formatted HTML alerts, with automatic backoff when the bot API rate limit is hit.

features.title: Circuit rotation and scheduling
features.body: The Tor control port is signalled to renew circuits on an interval so crawling does not stall on a dead circuit. Background jobs handle health checks, scheduled scraping, seed synchronisation and log cleanup.

technologies.purpose: Asynchronous event loop driving all concurrent network tasks
SOCKS5 proxy tunnelling and control-port circuit renewal
Non-blocking HTTP client for health checks and onion page downloads
DOM traversal, content extraction and link relevance scoring
Quantised GGUF models run locally, with no third-party API calls
Relevance classification, entity recognition and summarisation
Background jobs for health checks, scraping, seed sync and log cleanup
Persistent alert store with write-ahead logging and fast indexing
Asynchronous queue worker delivering formatted HTML alerts
Unit tests for parsers, URL normalisers and IOC patterns

project.running: The repository ships an installer that installs system dependencies, configures Tor to expose a SOCKS port and an authenticated control port bound to loopback, creates a virtual environment, downloads the model file, applies firewall rules and runs the test suite. It can be registered as a systemd service or run manually from the command line. A 4 GB machine is the floor for CPU inference with the 1.5B model, and CUDA acceleration is detected and used automatically when a compatible GPU is present.

project.scope: The project’s own disclaimer restricts it to authorised threat intelligence collection, defensive monitoring and academic research, and asks operators to satisfy the laws that apply to them. It is built for that purpose, and the same expectation applies here.

breach_reports.standfirst: Analysis of publicly reported security incidents. Where a finding rests on a threat actor’s own claims or on material they published, it is labelled as such rather than presented as a confirmed fact.
breach_reports.method_lede: Each report separates what was claimed, what was published, and what can actually be read from the exposed evidence. Where the source makes no distinction, this archive says so rather than filling the gap.

preamble.label: How to read this report.
preamble.text: The material below is drawn from a public breach listing associated with the ransomware group **Triple X**. Two different kinds of statement appear here and they are kept separate. The *actor profile* and the *techniques* are the group’s own characterisation of itself and of its intrusion method. The *exposed material* is what the group published. Neither has been independently confirmed by the affected organisation, and nothing here should be read as an admission by Bank of Baroda or a confirmed breach finding on its part.

observations.lead: The listing pointed at a directory index on the bank’s own infrastructure rather than at a copied file store:
observations.note: Read as a technical observation rather than a confirmed compromise: the published material points to an exposed directory index on a web server, and to documents that were publicly reachable through it. Whether access was authorised, misconfigured or obtained by other means is not established by the listing itself.
